message:
The 1.9 Hz first mode lies inside the critical vertical range so comfort governs, Manager.

In plain words normal walking can resonate the deck and the Human-Induced Vibration of Steel Structures, defined as Human-Induced Vibration of Steel Structures (HIVOSS), bands apply. I take from the Human-Induced Vibration on Lightweight Footbridges — 2024 (E19) that 1.9 Hz falls inside the 1.25 to 2.3 Hz critical vertical range, and I hold Maximum comfort below 0.5 m/s2, Medium comfort 0.5 to 1.0 m/s2, Minimum comfort 1.0 to 2.5 m/s2 and Unacceptable above 2.5 m/s2 from the comfort-target concept (C13) backed by the Low-Cost Angular-Velocity Measurements for Sustainable Dynamic Identification of Pedestrian Footbridges: A Case Study of the Footbridge in Gdynia (Poland) (E33).

Holding Maximum instead of Medium costs disproportionate hardware for little perceived gain, Manager.

In plain words chasing below 0.5 m/s2 from the calculated 0.67 m/s2 would need more mass, more units and harder under-deck work. The retrofitted 0.668 m/s2 from the retrofitted-acceleration calculation (E44) settling at 0.67 m/s2 in the crowd build-up simulation (E45) is 0.068 times gravity and everyday footbridge feel, against bare 8.28 m/s2 from the bare-acceleration calculation (E43) at 0.844 times gravity almost body weight and clearly outside everyday feel, so Medium is the buildable target for the twin 400 kg units serviced from below by Below Bridge Access Vehicle, defined as Below Bridge Access Vehicle (BBAV), from the inspection-access rule (E49).

I confirm from comfort what Retrofit Integration and Construction Lead takes from the A Review on Comfort of Pedestrian Bridges Under Human-Induced Vibrations and Tuned Mass Damper Control Technologies - PMC (E48), Structural Dynamicist and Bridge Retrofit Engineer.

In plain words spaced tunes hold the band when crowds are random, not only at exact resonance. The finding that a Multiple Tuned Mass Damper, defined as Multiple Tuned Mass Damper (MTMD), system demonstrates stronger robustness when dealing with random pedestrian loads means from my discipline that the detuned twin pair holds Medium under drift and random load, proven by the instrumented Class III crowd walk-through in my acceptance run (C29) where I borrow method from the Chapter 15 PDF (E60) while the bands set pass or fail.

My position is ready, because Medium with measured proof and from-below maintenance is comfortable, robust and buildable without changing the deck look.
